title: August and the Oath
premise: Freya Thackeray, a royal food-taster whose body has been slowly poisoned into immunity, has hidden his small magic for three years in Vellmark, a city that outlawed the gift after the old kingdom of Aurelan was erased from every map and memory but his. When the crown's witch-hunt begins, Freya learns he carries an inherited oath: the last living key to Aurelan's door, which only opens while its bearer still remembers the country. Hunted by the taster-master who trained him and shadowed by a memory-thief who wants the door for herself, Freya must choose between drinking the final poison that will make him untouchable—and erase his memories forever—or walking through the door as himself. In the end he gives up his own past to carry Aurelan's forward, stepping through with nothing but the oath intact.
about_author: Rafael Dunmore is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working kitchens in cities that no longer appear on tourist maps. He writes about hunger, inheritance, and the countries we carry inside us.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Morning in the palace kitchens: Freya sips arsenic-laced broth without flinching, then sells a luck-charm to a laundress in the market. He catalogs what he remembers of Aurelan in a hidden notebook. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the sense that safety is borrowed, not owned.

chapters.title: Small Charms, Heavy Prices
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A child pays Freya with a button to charm her sick mother's tea; the magic works, barely. His fence, Odell, warns him someone has been asking about 'the boy who tastes.' Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into fear—every kindness leaves a trail.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Criers announce the Gift-Hunt: registration, reward, and the pyre for refusers. Freya watches a hedge-witch dragged from a bakery and does nothing. That night he burns half his notebook. Emotional beat: shame—the first cost of survival is complicity.

chapters.title: Master Corvane
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The taster-master who trained him summons him, all courtesy, and offers protection in exchange for naming other gifted. Freya realizes Corvane has always known what he is. Emotional beat: the trap of patronage—his invisibility was someone else's leash all along.

chapters.title: What the Notebook Kept
chapters.summary: POV Freya, with a flashback chapter of young Freya and his grandmother teaching him the Oath-words over bread and salt. He rereads the surviving pages and finds a map fragment pointing to the Saltgate. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose—memory as inheritance, not burden.

chapters.title: The Memory-Thief
chapters.summary: POV Sable, introduced. A thief who eats memories for coin senses a country-sized prize somewhere in the city and begins hunting its scent through pawnshops and confessionals. Emotional beat: predatory patience—an antagonist who is charming, hungry, and utterly without guilt.

chapters.title: Saltgate at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya finds the gate—a door of black salt set into the harbor wall—but it will not open; the Oath demands a price he doesn't yet understand. Corvane's hunters nearly catch him; a stranger with grey eyes pulls him clear. Emotional beat: hope deferred—the door exists, but so does the hunt.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Freya. His rescuer is Ives, a disgraced royal cartographer who once mapped Aurelan and owes Freya's grandmother a life-debt. Ives explains the Oath: the door opens only for one who remembers, and it takes something in exchange. Emotional beat: wary alliance—two men bound by a dead country.

chapters.title: A Country No One Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ives. Ives narrates the erasure: how Aurelan was unmade from maps, records, and minds, leaving only its keys. He tests Freya's memories and is shaken by how much survives. Emotional beat: wonder and horror—Freya is not hiding from history; he is history.

chapters.title: The Second Dish
chapters.summary: POV Freya. To buy time, Freya returns to the palace, playing loyal taster while stealing Corvane's ledger of registered names—including children. Sable, posing as a clerk, tastes his memories in passing and confirms the prize. Emotional beat: double life tightening—betrayal on both sides of the same table.

chapters.title: Odell's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Odell is arrested for harboring charms; interrogators offer him Freya's name. Odell stays silent and hangs. Freya watches from a crowd, unable to intervene. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt sharpened into resolve—he will not be saved by other people's silence again.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable corners Freya and offers a trade: she'll show him the true price of the door if he lets her taste one memory of Aurelan. He refuses; she takes a small one anyway—a summer kitchen, gone. Emotional beat: violation—the hunt is no longer only for his body.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Corvane reveals he was born in Aurelan and chose erasure to survive; he hunts the gifted to prove his loyalty and hates Freya for keeping what he surrendered. He gives Freya until the equinox. Emotional beat: mirror and menace—the man Freya could become.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burned
chapters.summary: POV Ives. Ives and Freya destroy the registry, freeing dozens of named families and igniting riots in the low quarter. The act makes them famous; invisibility ends. Emotional beat: liberation with a fuse attached—they've traded safety for a head start.

chapters.title: What the Door Takes
chapters.summary: POV Freya. At Saltgate, blood and salt reveal the price: the door consumes the opener's own memories, leaving the Oath behind like a coat. Freya understands why his grandmother never went through. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the choice is between self and duty.

chapters.title: The Equinox Hunt
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Corvane's riders sweep the city; Ives is captured buying passage. Sable, having tasted enough of Aurelan to crave the rest, offers to lead Freya through the cordon—for the whole country this time. Emotional beat: desperation forcing strange bargains.

chapters.title: Poison as Armor
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya drinks Corvane's final proving-dose deliberately, gambling his trained immunity buys him an hour beyond the antidote's reach. It works; he walks out of the palace under the hunters' noses. Emotional beat: triumph built on self-harm—the taster's art turned inward.

chapters.title: Ives on the Block
chapters.summary: POV Ives. In custody, Ives feeds Corvane false details of the door's location, buying Freya a night. Facing the pyre, he recites Aurelan's borders from memory, making the crowd doubt their maps. Emotional beat: defiance as gift—one man's last lesson.

chapters.title: Saltgate at High Tide
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya and Sable reach the door together; she tries to take the Oath by force, but the door rejects a thief—it opens only for the willing. Freya begins paying: his mother's face, his first winter, his name. Emotional beat: sacrifice made real, memory by memory.

chapters.title: The Last Thing He Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Stripped nearly blank, Freya retains one chosen memory—the Oath itself—and steps through as Sable screams at the closing door. On the far side lies Aurelan, alive, waiting for its key. Emotional beat: arrival hollowed and holy—he saved a country by losing himself.

chapters.title: The Man Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Freya (fragmented). In Aurelan, Freya relearns his name from the Oath-words themselves; the people greet him as heir-key, not hero. He plants his grandmother's bread-salt ritual in new soil. Emotional beat: rebirth without restoration—an inheritance accepted at last.

chapters.title: August and the Oath
chapters.summary: POV alternating, epilogue. Years later, a food-taster trains a gifted child in Aurelan's rebuilt kitchens, teaching both immunity and memory. Across the sea, rumor says a grey-eyed cartographer survived the pyre. Emotional beat: continuity—the price paid becomes the seed planted, and the story closes where it began: a spoon, a mouthful, a remembered country.
